content.text: A gambling game's been set up in a place unfamiliar to you. Soon, you'll be invited to join the table as well.

branch.text: Hmph ... you seem to have grown quite assertive. But remember this: as a newcomer to the table, you have no privilege to make demands or probe for information unless you're looking to be targeted and isolated.

You have to lose a few rounds—pay your "entry fee." Only then can you start to learn the secrets of those at the table. The players' backgrounds, the dealer's habits, and the truth behind the highest-stakes gambler.
It's baffling to me. Why would anyone travel halfway across the world just to throw away their money?
That was a rhetorical question. But thanks for answering.
You're right; the allure of winning is irresistible, even in a game of chance. People blow on the dice, clutch a rabbit's foot, or murmur a prayer, foolishly believing they can sway the outcome.
Tsk, disappointing indeed. To think you're entangled in such empty words.
Some are so captivated by these grandiose phrases that they feel empowered when using them. Despite their vapidity, it makes them feel important.

Oh, quite the opposite. The odds are rarely equal. Your opponents could have any number of advantages stuffed up their sleeves—a larger stack of chips, easier winning conditions, or even the power to change the rules. Want a fair game? You've got to fight for it, by any means necessary.
The white suits always play it safe, carefully hedging their bets, while the black robes plot to overturn the table.
Clever? More like cretinous and atrocious.
Once the table's flipped, there'll be nothing but chaos. Who would bother to set it right again? No one.

items.text: The Sleepless Man
Igor's Office
Admiral Igor rarely makes calls to Zeno headquarters, but the situation has become desperate.
Ah, Igor! How are things in São Paulo?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Worse than expected.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I have a small number of troops with me, but not enough to deal with the situation.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Things have gotten out of hand. At least one of the Apostles Brotherhood leaders has pledged allegiance to the Manus.
Tsk, Brotherhood? These new gangs just keep popping up, don't they? It's like cutting down sugarcane. Before you know it, another one's grown in its place.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Carlos has been murdered by his own subordinates. Even now, some of the deserters are with the Brotherhood.
This news is met with a prolonged silence.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Did you catch them?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Some have already been executed. The rest will be transferred to headquarters for interrogation.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Good. What assistance do you require, comrade?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: An army. A reliable one.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: An army? I'm afraid that's not possible. We simply don't have the men to spare.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: It doesn't need to be large.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Just dispatch my Sentinel Unit from Buenos Aires to São Paulo.
A loyal army led by the children he raised himself, composed of orphans of war born into Zeno's cause.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Or at the very least, send Ptolemy.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Ptolemy? Ah, one of your orphan "children." Hmm. That seems like a feasible solution.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Yes, his parents died fighting for Zeno. All my children are loyal to a fault.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Officer Carlos was shot in the head by one of his own men in this very office. I need soldiers I can trust.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Ah, so the fearless Igor is afraid of death, after all?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: An officer was killed by his own soldiers at his own base. This is an immense stain on Zeno's honor.
How little honor they have left. Igor clings to it like a leaf to a tree in winter.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Indeed. If everything goes according to plan, you'll see your unit shortly.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Now, it's just a matter of time.
The admiral tosses the dice in his hand. Up and down, up and down.
He receives the same oracle—the same answer—like the inscription on the Behistun monument. It is eternal. Unchanging.
"His heart is a hanging lyre, a hanging lyre ... gently plucked ... "
An ancient verse rises in the old admiral's memory.
Dark omens. Ill prophecies. It is all whispered from his lips.
I have seen the hawk chase the dove and the sun god pull his golden bowstring taut.
I watched as the wooden horse was welcomed into our territories, and the sacred fountain flowed with the blood of the fledgling birds.
Ah, but a man of steely mind and lofty pride knows ...
That his city will endure. Its walls will stand strong. It will be as steadfast as the earth's core.
What wickedness ...
Now, the die is cast ...
The pale shroud will devour him, and he will be enveloped by the grim night.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: All for a better future.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: A better future for everyone ...
On this rain-soaked night, this is the only answer.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Admiral.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Come in.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Yesterday, we received word from the Timekeeper that Dr. Dores has been abducted by the Apostles Brotherhood. She should be coordinating with Lopera to set up a rescue operation as we speak.
She breathes a sigh of relief. The doctor may have been abducted, but at least the Timekeeper is safe.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Also, that girl who escaped, Kimberly, is with the Timekeeper. She claims that she was released.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Just play along with her lie. There's no need to tell Lopera the truth.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The Brotherhood has demanded that we exchange the detained deserters for the doctor. Forgive me for issuing instructions without your consent, but if we refuse or ignore them, I'm afraid they'll—

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: They'll execute the doctor.
He knows full well the ways of these thugs.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: What arrangements did you make?
Moldir tenses up a little, unsure of how her father will react to her decision.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I told the Timekeeper that Zeno reinforcements would meet her at the Veterans' Residence.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Since Lopera is familiar with the place, I also asked her to scout out the rendezvous location.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: And, yes. I played along with Kimberly's lie. I-I assumed you would've done the same, Father.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Very good.
While the admiral refused to talk to anyone last night, his daughter had been modeling her actions after him.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Your squad will soon arrive. Take them to Lopera at the rendezvous point and bring the doctor back.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: A squad?
The admiral gazes out the window.
He scans the barren fort, the weathered stone, and the vines slowly wearing away at the walls. How did this come to be?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I've spoken with headquarters. All going well, Ptolemy and the unit will arrive soon.
Moldir's body relaxes a little, and a smile grows on her face.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I see. I can hardly remember the last time we were all together.
Her smile turns bittersweet.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Your father died in Abadan, in a war he had no obligation to fight in.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: It's far more glorious to die in the throes of battle than to wither away on a sickbed. He made an honorable sacrifice.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: How shameful that we would tarnish his honor.
Honor is a thing easily stained.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Let's begin with that young pilot, Lilya. Tell me, what do you think of her?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: She's well-trained, experienced, a straight shooter—similar to Lopera in many ways.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: She's a true Slav. Just like my brothers and sisters back home.
Stubborn, loyal, brave, and as unshakable as the frozen Siberian earth.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I suppose she's luckier than Lopera. Not destined to become a traitor like her.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Lopera's still a child, really.
The admiral closes his eyes as he remembers those who fought beside him.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: So many lives have been lost, in wars, in the "Storm."
They have all been enshrined in the Hall of Merit at headquarters.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: What do you think Lopera will do?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: She's your child, just like me. I think she will stand with us.
He smirks.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: You "think," do you?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Anyway, she's not important. Here, take a look at this.
An invitation.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I will not wear it.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Nor will you. I promise you, not one of us will wear this thing.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: The Preacher has given us a gift and shared with us an "oracle."

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: We will bring her something in return.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Fire and brimstone rained down from heaven, yet among the ruins we recovered the remnants of a miracle.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: A miracle that is living, breathing, and growing.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I can sense THEIR life force. I can hear THEIR whispers from within these ashes.
A lucid dream, a living death, a perished immortality.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Moldir, THEY are invincible.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Rather than endlessly throwing young soldiers' lives to the White Stone House ...

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I choose to stand with the true future.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I will always stand with you, Father.
TO BE CONTINUED…
